{{nihongo|'''Fujiuchi Shrine'''|藤内神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hitachi Province]].

'''Fujiuchi Shrine''' (????????) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|Q83273|qid=Q83273}}{{ill|Mito, Ibaraki|Q204249|qid=Q204249}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking}} it was a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
*'''{{ill|Futsunushi|fr|Futsunushi|it|Futsunushi|ja|経津主神|mni|ꯐꯨꯠꯁꯨꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Futsunushi|ru|Фуцунуси|zh|經津主神|qid=Q1107286|lt=Futsunushi-no-Mikoto}}'''

According to shrine tradition, Ch?b?zan, located about 5 km west of the shrine, is the sacred mountain of the enshrined deity Futsunushi-no-Mikoto. Ch?b?zan is also known as a candidate site of {{ill|Hodoki Mountain|Q48753472|qid=Q48753472}} recorded in the Naka District section of the ''{{ill|Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki|Q11481687|qid=Q11481687}}''.

=== History ===
=== Founding ===
According to shrine tradition, at dawn on {{ill|April 12|Q2499|qid=Q2499}} of Y?r? 5 ({{ill|721|Q23541|qid=Q23541}}), a divine light shone on Ch?b?zan. The light descended toward Fujii-go, astonishing the people, and on {{ill|June 15|Q2613|qid=Q2613}} they built the shrine hall. Another tradition says that during the {{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}} era, Futsunushi-no-Mikoto was invited from {{ill|Katori Jingū|Q372380|qid=Q372380}} by divine oracle.

=== Overview ===
It is listed in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'' as "Fujiuchi Shrine in Naka District, Hitachi Province" and is treated as one of its candidate shrines. In K?hei 5 ({{ill|1062|Q19396|qid=Q19396}}), {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|Q32613|qid=Q32613}} is said to have gathered one hundred thousand troops on the northwestern ridge of this shrine on his way north, prayed here for lasting military fortune, received a branch of wisteria from before the shrine to use as a riding crop, and advanced; the place where troops were assembled is called "J?manbara."

Before the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}, it was called "Fujiuchi Daimy?jin." When the shrine buildings burned down in the {{ill|Daiei (era)|Q1193564|qid=Q1193564}} era (1521-1528), they were rebuilt in Kan'ei 5 ({{ill|1628|Q6840|qid=Q6840}}) by {{ill|Akita Sanesue|Q4701233|qid=Q4701233}} of the {{ill|Shishido Domain|Q3034528|qid=Q3034528|lt=Shishido domain}}, and rebuilt again in the Genroku era (1688-1704) by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|de|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|es|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|fa|توکوگاوا میتسوکونی|fr|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|id|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|it|Mito Kōmon|ja|徳川光圀|ko|도쿠가와 미쓰쿠니|pl|Mitsukuni Tokugawa|pt|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ru|Токугава Мицукуни|simple|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|sl|Tokugawa Micukuni|ug|توكۇگاۋا مىتسۇكۇنى|uk|Токуґава Міцукуні|zh|德川光圀|qid=Q1194944}} of the {{ill|Mito Domain|de|Mito (Han)|fa|قلمرو میتو|fr|Domaine de Mito|ja|水戸藩|ko|미토번|pt|Domínio de Mito|ru|Мито (княжество)|uk|Міто-хан|wuu|水户藩|zh|水戶藩|qid=Q1146904}}, showing strong patronage from nearby lords. In Meiji 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), it was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}} in the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}.
